# Implementation Plan: Agent-comms Scope A live cross-machine wiring
<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"agent-comms-scope-a-live-cross-machine-wiring"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-08. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/agent-comms-scope-a-live-cross-machine-wiring/plan.md`.*

## Overview

Scope A of agent-comms (two daemons on different machines, paired to the same operator GitHub identity, talking end-to-end over Microsoft Dev Tunnels) exists today as **design + skeleton only** (`plans/agent-comms-design.md` §5.6 explicitly defers live wiring). The crypto, wire schema, router, ingest route, peer transport, and Dev-Tunnels discovery are all implemented and unit-tested, and the **inbound** path is already wired end-to-end (`packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/api.ts:115` registers `agentCommsIngestRoutes` with the daemon-injected handler on the hosted tunnel listener). What is missing for a **live** cross-machine round-trip is: (1) the **outbound** half — `dispatchAgentCommsEnvelope` is only ever given `deliverLocal`, so every Scope A send returns 501; (2) an automated proof that a real signed+sealed envelope survives the full chain to a remote daemon's mailbox; and (3) enforcement of the already-defined `requiresOperatorApproval` predicate so a peer cannot silently trigger a spawn on a remote daemon.

This plan closes those three gaps while preserving §5.4 two-layer auth and §5.3 discovery byte-for-byte, keeping Microsoft Dev Tunnels the sole channel for data + signaling + rendezvous + discovery + auth. It locks the **D-004 port model to CO-LOCATED** (ingest rides the existing single forwarded happy-server tunnel port), which—critically—means the `devtunnel host` lifecycle is **already running** (`DevTunnelsDaemonProvider.loadHostTunnel` → `startHost` on daemon boot), so deliverable (1) reduces to verification + hardening rather than a new host stack.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context
- **Inbound is already live.** `packages/happy-server/sources/app/api/api.ts:115` registers `agentCommsIngestRoutes(typed, { handler: options.agentCommsIngest })` on the tunnel listener only (`auth !== "loopback"`). `packages/happy-cli/src/types/happy-server.d.ts:42-90` already declares `agentCommsIngest`. The daemon-injected closure `packages/happy-cli/src/daemon/run.ts:219-241` does the full §5.4 chain: `requirePinnedPeer` → fingerprint+pubkey match → `verifyEnvelopeSignature` → `openSealedBody` → `advanceAgentCommsRelay` (relay id `daemon-<machineId>`) → target-machine check → `appendMessage`.
- **Outbound is the gap.** `packages/happy-cli/src/daemon/controlServer.ts:325-336` calls `dispatchAgentCommsEnvelope` with only `deliverLocal`; `packages/happy-cli/src/agentComms/router.ts:196-203` throws `agent_comms_remote_transport_unavailable` (→ 501 at controlServer.ts:342) for scope A when `deliverRemote` is absent.
- **Transport skeleton exists but is fed nothing.** `packages/happy-cli/src/agentComms/peerTransport.ts:49-84` `DevTunnelsPeerTransport.send()` accepts an ALREADY-`SignedSealedEnvelope`, mints a connect token, and POSTs with `X-Tunnel-Authorization`. Nothing builds that signed+sealed envelope on the outbound side today, and `listReachablePeers()` returns tunnel hints with **no authoritative `machineId`**.
- **Approval predicate exists, enforced nowhere.** `router.ts:187-189` `requiresOperatorApproval(envelope)` = scope A && (channel `spawn` || kind `spawn-request`). The ingest closure (`run.ts:219-241`) `appendMessage`s every envelope unconditionally — it never branches on spawn. The MCP sender side `packages/happy-cli/src/codex/agentCommsBridge.ts:201-218` short-circuits a foreign-`machineId` `agent_comms.spawn` to a `deferred-scope-a-spawn` error (no live request sent).
- **Crypto / keys reuse as-is.** `peerAuth.ts:53-131` (`signEnvelope`/`verifyEnvelopeSignature`/`sealBody`/`openSealedBody`/`pinPeerKeys`/`requirePinnedPeer`, pin store `<happyHomeDir>/agent-comms/peers.json` keyed by machineId, holding ed25519/ecdh pub + fingerprint + `pinnedAt`, **no tunnel hint**). `keypairManager.ts:31-38` stores keys DIRECTLY under `<happyHomeDir>` (`server-key.{pub,priv}`, `ecdh-key.{pub,priv}`). Wire schema `packages/happy-wire/src/agentComms.ts:10-63` (`MAX_HOPS=4`, channel `message|spawn`, kind `request|reply|notify|spawn-request|spawn-result`).
- **Tunnel host already runs.** `devTunnelsDaemonProvider.ts:74-79` `loadHostTunnel` calls `manager.startHost(config, port)`; `tunnelManager.ts:317-330` `startHost` spawns one `devtunnel host <tunnelId>`. `listOperatorTunnels` (tunnelManager.ts:332-339) / `mintConnectToken` (341-352) are stable and must stay untouched. `ensurePort` uses `--port-number`.
- **Harness precedent.** `packages/happy-cli/src/agentComms/mailbox.crossProcess.integration.test.ts` — `*.integration.test.ts` in the SERIAL vitest project `integration-agent-comms` (maxWorkers:1), forks real OS processes with a temp `HAPPY_HOME_DIR` and contends on the cross-process mailbox lock. This is the model for the two-daemon harness.

### Technical Constraints
- **Dev Tunnels is the SOLE channel** for data + signaling + rendezvous + discovery + auth. Nothing may transit the phone, the Happy app, a central happy-server broker/relay, or any third party.
- **Backend must never inspect `X-Tunnel-Authorization`** — the gateway strips it (happy-server/AGENTS.md). Backend-observable auth is only TOFU-pinned Ed25519 + ECDH sealed body.
- **`listOperatorTunnels()` and `mintConnectToken()` must stay byte-for-byte unchanged** (§5.3), and `peerTransport.ingestUrl()` selection must not change (§5.3 discovery invariant). Never derive a peer `machineId` by stripping `codexu-<hostname>` (§8.2).
- Single-port `TunnelConfig`/`MachineLocallyPersistedState`/`DaemonTunnelProvider`; embedded one-user-per-process happy-server; Windows `devtunnel` CLI uses `--port-number`, private tunnels only (no anonymous flags). All ingest/approval/spawn paths must be idempotent (clients retry).

## Approach

### Architecture

**D-004 decision — CO-LOCATED ingest on the existing happy-server tunnel port (the reportable decision).**
4-source convergence (architect, codex xhigh, copilot xhigh, first-hand source read). Ingest already rides the single forwarded port that the daemon's `devtunnel host` already publishes and on which the embedded happy-server (carrying `agentCommsIngestRoutes`) is bound. Co-located therefore:
- keeps §5.3 `devtunnel list --json` discovery **and** `peerTransport.ingestUrl()` byte-for-byte unchanged (the chosen URL is the one forwarded port + `/agent-comms/ingest`);
- requires **no** new `devtunnel host` stack and **no** widening of `machine.json`/`TunnelConfig`/provider to multi-port;
- keeps the D-001 (`agent-comms-serverless-scope-a-discovery`) seam compatible **regardless of ship order** — D-001 is not shipped, so this task targets the current happy-server ingest route; a future D-001 listener can take over `/agent-comms/ingest` behind the same tunnel port without the outbound side changing, because outbound depends only on `ingestUrl()` resolving to `<forwarded-base>/agent-comms/ingest`.

Rejected: a SECOND forwarded port for ingest. It would force `ports[]` disambiguation, change `ingestUrl()` selection and §5.3 semantics, and widen single-port state/provider types — all to solve a problem (decoupling ingest off happy-server) that belongs to D-001, not this task. To keep that future cheap, the new peer-target type (US-002) is structured so a second-port switch is a localized follow-up.

**D-005 decision — peer→tunnel resolver from operator-authored peer config joined to `listOperatorTunnels()` at send time.** The pin store has no tunnel hint and `listReachablePeers()` has no authoritative `machineId`, so a new resolver maps `machineId → PeerTransportTarget{ tunnelId, ingestUrl, peerEcdhPublicKey }` by reading the operator-authored/TOFU-pinned peer record (extended with an optional `tunnelName`/`tunnelId` hint) and resolving it against `listOperatorTunnels()` output — **without modifying `listOperatorTunnels`/`mintConnectToken`**, and never deriving `machineId` from the tunnel name.

**The §5.4 verification chain and §5.3 discovery are preserved byte-for-byte; only the outbound *direction* is added.** What "byte-for-byte" protects is the **backend-observable verification** (`peerAuth.ts` Ed25519 verify + ECDH sealed-body open against the TOFU-pinned key, in the existing order) and the §5.3 discovery surface (`listOperatorTunnels`/`mintConnectToken`/`ingestUrl()`), none of whose bodies change. Outbound reuses `signEnvelope` + `sealBody` (sealing to the pinned peer ECDH key) — the mirror of the inbound checks, not a new scheme. Note on first-contact TOFU: §5.4 *describes* an automatic first-contact public-key exchange, but that exchange was never implemented (it is skeleton, and §5.6/§8.1 already treat peer pinning as a satisfied prerequisite). v1 therefore requires peers to be **pre-pinned** (operator-authored `peers.json` or a one-time pin step); this is consistent with §8.1's prerequisite and is **not** a regression of the §5.4 verification contract. Automatic first-contact exchange remains a documented follow-up.

### Implementation Strategy
1. **US-001 (decision + docs):** Record D-004=co-located and D-005=peer-resolver in `plans/agent-comms-design.md` (flip §5.6 "deferred" to "landed" for the wired pieces; fix the stale `<happyHomeDir>/tofu/server-key` path to the real `<happyHomeDir>/server-key.*`; document the pre-pinned-peer prerequisite + the automated harness + the retained manual §8 smoke).
2. **US-002 (peer resolver):** new `packages/happy-cli/src/agentComms/peerResolver.ts` — peer-config schema (tunnel hint + reuse of the pin record's crypto), `resolvePeerTarget(machineId)` joining pins + `listOperatorTunnels()`. Unit-tested with injected tunnel list + fixture pins. **Repin-preservation (flagged by review):** if the tunnel hint (`tunnelName`/`tunnelId`) and the `approvedForSpawn` flag live in the `peers.json` pin record, `pinPeerKeys()` (`peerAuth.ts:102-119`) currently reconstructs the record from keys/fingerprint/pinnedAt only and would **drop** operator-authored fields on repin — US-002 must carry those fields through a repin (merge, not overwrite).
3. **US-003 (outbound `deliverRemote`):** wire a `deliverRemote(envelope)` into `controlServer.ts` `/agent-comms/send` that resolves the target (US-002), seals `envelope.body` to the peer ECDH key, signs the sealed envelope, attaches local public keys (`senderKeys`), and calls `DevTunnelsPeerTransport.send()`. Scope A stops returning 501 when the peer resolves; unresolved/unpinned peers still fail closed. **Note (channel/kind plumbing — flagged by review):** the `/agent-comms/send` route body schema (`controlServer.ts:277-293`) currently accepts only `kind: request|reply|notify` and has **no `channel` field**, and the `sendAgentMessage()` helper (`controlClient.ts:126-141`) cannot pass `channel`. US-003 widens the route schema + helper to carry `channel: 'message'|'spawn'` and the `spawn-request`/`spawn-result` kinds so US-005's spawn-request can traverse the same outbound path; keep `message`/`request` the default so existing callers are unaffected.
4. **US-004 (host lifecycle verification, co-located):** confirm the already-hosted tunnel serves `/agent-comms/ingest` (co-located) and that `startHost`/route registration cover it. **Readiness ordering (flagged by review):** `dualListenerBinding.ts:38` starts `devtunnel host` BEFORE the embedded tunnel listener binds at `dualListenerBinding.ts:72`, so any readiness check must target the **local** tunnel listener *after* `tunnel.start()` (or the Dev Tunnels URL only with a minted connect token) — never the public URL before the listener is up. Any such probe MUST be **log-only / non-fatal** (it depends on the external Dev Tunnels gateway and must never block or crash daemon boot); deterministic CI proof comes from the existing `startHost` + route-registration tests, not a live probe. Confirm clean host stop on shutdown. Small — the host process already runs.
5. **US-005 (approval gate + live spawn-request):** enforce `requiresOperatorApproval` in the `run.ts` ingest closure with a **concrete, verifiable contract**:
   - **Spawn-request body schema:** define the `spawn-request` envelope `body` shape (agent, cwd/path, role, plugins, initialMessage, model, permissionMode, effortLevel — mirroring `SpawnToolArgs` in `agentCommsBridge.ts:91-102`) and its mapping to `SpawnSessionFromSessionRpcOptions['config']` (`spawnSessionFromSession.ts`); the spawned child's `parentSessionId` is the *remote* daemon's relay session (cross-machine parent links are not walked by `validateSpawnAncestry`, which stops at cross-machine ancestors).
   - **Default-deny + allowlist:** spawn-channel / `spawn-request` envelopes are denied unless the sender `machineId` carries an explicit `approvedForSpawn: true` flag in the peer config (US-002's peer record). Non-allowlisted requests are recorded to a pending-approvals file (`<happyHomeDir>/agent-comms/pending-spawns.json`) and **never executed**.
   - **Idempotency:** key executed spawns by `envelope.id` (and `correlationId` when present) in a durable dedupe set so an ingest retry of the same `spawn-request` does **not** spawn a duplicate child; a retry returns the prior result.
   - **Result envelope:** on approval+execution, reply with a `spawn-result` envelope (success/error) back to the requester via the outbound path.
   - **Sender side:** wire the MCP `agent_comms.spawn` foreign-`machineId` path (`agentCommsBridge.ts:201-218`) to send a real `spawn-request` envelope through the US-003 outbound path instead of the `deferred-scope-a-spawn` stub.
   - **Dependency wiring (flagged by review):** the `agentCommsIngest` closure is constructed early (`run.ts:219-241`) but `spawnSessionFromSessionHandler` is created much later (`run.ts:939-956`). The gate cannot call the spawn handler directly at construction time; inject it through a deferred/promise indirection mirroring the existing late-binding pattern at `run.ts:849-859` (resolve the handler reference after it exists, before any approved spawn-request is processed).
   v1 ships **allowlist-only** (the `approvedForSpawn` flag IS the operator approval); an interactive/queue-consume operator approval UI on top of the pending-spawns file is an explicit follow-up.
6. **US-006 (automated two-daemon harness):** a hermetic `*.integration.test.ts` that boots two embedded happy-server instances (or injects the ingest handler) on loopback with two temp `HAPPY_HOME_DIR`s, pre-pins fixture keys both ways, injects a loopback `FetchLike` (+ `CommandRunner`), and drives the full chain (sign → seal → POST → route → verify → open → relay-advance → `appendMessage`) asserting the message lands in the REMOTE mailbox; plus a spawn-request round-trip asserting the approval gate blocks an un-allowlisted peer and admits an allowlisted one (and an idempotent-retry case). **Harness-auth boundary (flagged by review):** the Fastify route uses `app.authenticate` and is registered only on the tunnel-auth listener (`api.ts:109-115`), so the hermetic crypto round-trip should drive the **injected `agentCommsIngest` handler directly** (the real `peerAuth` chain, no gateway), with a **separate** route-level test covering the Fastify schema + `routeHopValidation` + 503/400 boundary. Add an opt-in real-`devtunnel` smoke script for the genuinely un-hermetic part (gateway connect-token admission). Draft the harness interface early so it drives the route/client/spawn-handler shapes rather than discovering them last.

## Scope
### In Scope
- D-004 (co-located) + D-005 (peer resolver) decisions and their wiring.
- Live outbound Scope A delivery (`deliverRemote`) and removal of the unconditional 501.
- Operator-approval gate (default-deny + allowlist + pending-approval) enforced before any remote spawn executes, plus the live `spawn-request` sender path.
- Automated hermetic two-daemon round-trip + approval-gate integration test; opt-in real-devtunnel smoke.
- Byte-for-byte preservation of the §5.4 **backend-observable verification chain** (`peerAuth` Ed25519 verify + ECDH sealed-body open against the TOFU-pinned key, in the existing order) and the §5.3 discovery **public contract** (`listOperatorTunnels`/`mintConnectToken`/`ingestUrl()` behavior + public signatures unchanged).
- Doc sync in `plans/agent-comms-design.md`.

### Out of Scope
- A SECOND forwarded ingest port / multi-port `TunnelConfig` (D-004 rejected alternative; future D-001 concern).
- Removing the embedded happy-server from the daemon, or moving ingest to a happy-cli-owned listener (that is D-001, a separate task).
- Relocating `AgentCommsIngestBodySchema` / hop validation to `@slopus/happy-wire` (D-001 owns it; keep the handler contract compatible).
- Automatic TOFU first-contact key exchange (v1 requires pre-pinned peers, per §8.1).
- Pub-sub fan-out; codex submodule edits; any non-Dev-Tunnels transport.

## Risk Areas
- **Auth-order / sealing regressions.** The outbound seal+sign must exactly mirror the inbound open+verify (canonicalization, base64, nonce). A mismatch silently fails decryption. Mitigation: US-006 exercises the real `peerAuth` round-trip; reuse the existing helpers, do not re-derive canonicalization.
- **Accidentally changing discovery/URL selection** (the highest-risk seam per the architect): keep `ingestUrl()` and `listOperatorTunnels`/`mintConnectToken` untouched; the resolver only *consumes* them.
- **Approval gate landing too late** (after a child process starts) defeats it. The gate must sit in the ingest closure before any `spawnSessionFromSession` call, fail closed, and be idempotent under retry.
- **Hermeticity of the harness.** The real `devtunnel host` + gateway connect-token admission cannot run in CI; assert those via `TunnelManager` unit tests + the opt-in manual smoke, and keep the automated test injecting `FetchLike`/`CommandRunner` so CI never touches the network.
- **Sender-id shape on append.** The inbound relay passes `relayedEnvelope.from.sessionId` (bare) to `appendMessage`; confirm this matches the mailbox `SESSION_ID_REGEX` for cross-machine senders.
- **Idempotent remote spawn.** Allowlisted `spawn-request` retries (ingest clients retry) could spawn duplicate children unless executed spawns are deduped by `envelope.id`/`correlationId`. The gate must record executed spawn ids durably and return the prior `spawn-result` on retry.
- **Windows** `devtunnel` `--port-number` and private-tunnel-only posture; Git-Bash test invocation (`npm_config_script_shell=bash`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **D-004 is recorded as co-located** in `plans/agent-comms-design.md`, with the rationale and the D-001 seam-compatibility note; the stale `<happyHomeDir>/tofu/server-key` reference is corrected to `<happyHomeDir>/server-key.*`.
- A Scope A `agent_comms.send` to a pinned, resolvable foreign peer **delivers a real signed+sealed envelope** that the remote daemon verifies (Ed25519), opens (ECDH), relay-advances, and lands via `mailbox.appendMessage`; the control route no longer returns 501 for a resolvable peer. **Verified by** the US-006 automated two-daemon integration test asserting the remote mailbox contains the plaintext body.
- The **behavior and public contract** of `listOperatorTunnels()`, `mintConnectToken()`, and `peerTransport.ingestUrl()` selection are **unchanged** — a behavior-preserving refactor is acceptable, and for a single-port tunnel the chosen URL is still `<portUri>/agent-comms/ingest`; existing `peerTransport.test.ts`/`tunnelManager` tests still pass unmodified. **Verified by** test pass + diff review.
- The §5.4 backend-observable verification is preserved: unknown peer, fingerprint mismatch, signature failure, and sealed-body open failure each **reject before `appendMessage`**. **Verified by** harness negative cases.
- A cross-machine `agent_comms.spawn` (channel `spawn`/kind `spawn-request`) from a **non-allowlisted** peer is **denied and never spawns** (recorded to `pending-spawns.json`); from an **allowlisted** peer (`approvedForSpawn: true`) it maps the spawn-request body to `SpawnSessionFromSessionRpcOptions` and calls `spawnSessionFromSession`, then returns a `spawn-result` envelope so the requester learns the spawned session id (or error). A duplicate ingest of the same `spawn-request` (`envelope.id`/`correlationId`) does **not** spawn a second child (idempotent). **Verified by** US-006 gate + idempotency cases. The MCP `agent_comms.spawn` foreign-`machineId` path sends a real `spawn-request` envelope (no longer the `deferred-scope-a-spawn` stub).
- Dev Tunnels remains the sole channel (no phone/app/central-server/relay code added). **Verified by** diff review.
- `pnpm --filter happy typecheck`, `pnpm --filter happy test`, `pnpm --filter happy-server typecheck`, and `pnpm --filter happy-server test` pass.

- **US-001** — D-004/D-005 decisions + `plans/agent-comms-design.md` doc sync (incl. stale key-path fix). (small, docs)
- **US-002** — `peerResolver.ts`: machineId→`PeerTransportTarget` from operator/pinned peer config + `listOperatorTunnels()`; peer-config schema. (medium, happy-cli)
- **US-003** — outbound `deliverRemote` live wiring (seal+sign+send) into `controlServer.ts`/`run.ts` + widen `/agent-comms/send` route schema and `controlClient.ts` `sendAgentMessage()` to carry `channel`/spawn kinds; remove unconditional 501. (medium, happy-cli)
- **US-004** — co-located host-lifecycle verification + log-only/non-fatal readiness (local listener after `tunnel.start()`). (small, happy-cli)
- **US-005** — operator-approval gate in ingest closure (default-deny + `approvedForSpawn` allowlist + `pending-spawns.json` + idempotent dedupe + deferred spawn-handler injection + `spawn-result` reply) + live `spawn-request` sender in `agentCommsBridge.ts`. (medium, happy-cli)
- **US-006** — automated hermetic two-daemon round-trip + approval-gate integration test; opt-in real-devtunnel smoke. (large, happy-cli test)

## Suggested Decomposition

These stories are deeply coupled across the same happy-cli files (`run.ts`, `controlServer.ts`, `peerTransport.ts`, `agentComms/*`), so the realistic execution is **serial in one impl member**, with only the docs story safely parallelizable. Clusters below reflect dependency order, not a recommendation to fan out.

### Cluster: docs-and-decision
- Stories: US-001
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`plans/agent-comms-design.md`]; risk=low
- `execution_mode` rationale: Touches only the design doc; can run in parallel with code stories without conflict.

### Cluster: outbound-core
- Stories: US-002, US-003, US-004
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: None (code-independent of US-001)
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[`packages/happy-cli/src/daemon/run.ts`, `packages/happy-cli/src/agentComms/peerTransport.ts`]; exclusive=[`peerResolver.ts`, `controlServer.ts`, tunnel readiness]; risk=high
- `execution_mode` rationale: US-003 consumes US-002's resolver and both edit `run.ts`/`peerTransport.ts`; must be serialized within one member. US-004 is small and touches adjacent tunnel/daemon startup — keep it in the same serial member to avoid `run.ts` conflicts.

### Cluster: approval-and-harness

- Phase: 3
- Depends on: outbound-core

## Open Questions
- **D-005 storage:** does the per-peer tunnel hint live in the existing `peers.json` pin record (extending its schema) or in a companion operator config? Recommendation: extend the pin record with an optional `tunnelName`/`tunnelId`; resolve to a live tunnel via `listOperatorTunnels()` at send time. (Decide in US-002.)
- **Pending-approval surfacing (RESOLVED → v1 allowlist-only):** v1 ships default-deny + the peer-config `approvedForSpawn` flag as the approval mechanism; non-allowlisted `spawn-request`s are recorded to `<happyHomeDir>/agent-comms/pending-spawns.json` and never executed. An interactive/queue-consume operator approval surface (loopback control endpoint / CLI subcommand) on top of that file is an explicit **follow-up**, NOT in this task's acceptance criteria.
- **US-006 ordering:** the harness lands after the outbound + approval contracts (US-003/US-005), but its interface should be drafted early enough to drive the route/client/spawn-handler shapes.
- **First-contact auto-pin** is deferred (v1 = pre-pinned peers per §8.1). Confirm this is acceptable for the live round-trip target, or whether a one-time pin-exchange utility is in scope.
